## Previously {#fm4-previously .fm-slide .fm-compound-recap }

\$2000 is invested at **6% p.a., compounded annually**. Find the balance after **3 years**.

```{=html}
<div class="split fm-recap-layout">
  <div class="column-block">
    <h3>Interest, then balance</h3>
    <p class="fm-recap-method"><span data-math="I=PRN,\quad R=0.06,\quad N=1"></span></p>
    <div class="fm-recap-year fragment" data-fragment-index="0">
      <strong>Year 1</strong>
      <div><span data-math="I=2000\times0.06\times1=120"></span><br><span data-math="2000+120=2120"></span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="fm-recap-year fragment" data-fragment-index="1">
      <strong>Year 2</strong>
      <div><span data-math="I=2120\times0.06\times1=127.20"></span><br><span data-math="2120+127.20=2247.20"></span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="fm-recap-year fragment" data-fragment-index="2">
      <strong>Year 3</strong>
      <div><span data-math="I=2247.20\times0.06\times1=134.832"></span><br><span data-math="2247.20+134.832=2382.032"></span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="column-block fragment" data-fragment-index="3">
    <h3>A 6% increase each period</h3>
    <p class="fm-recap-method">Multiply by <span data-math="1+\frac{6}{100}=1.06"></span></p>
    <div class="fm-recap-year"><strong>Year 1</strong><div><span data-math="2000\times1.06=2120"></span></div></div>
    <div class="fm-recap-year"><strong>Year 2</strong><div><span data-math="2120\times1.06=2247.20"></span></div></div>
    <div class="fm-recap-year"><strong>Year 3</strong><div><span data-math="2247.20\times1.06=2382.032"></span></div></div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="fragment takeaway fm-recap-summary" data-fragment-index="4">
  <span data-math="A=2000\times1.06\times1.06\times1.06=2000(1.06)^3\approx\$2382.03"></span>
</div>
```

::: notes
Revisit the \$2000 at 6% example from Lesson 3. First ask students to use $I=PRN$ for one year at a time, adding that year's interest to the balance before moving on. Reveal Years 1, 2 and 3 separately. Each calculation uses $N=1$ and the current balance as $P$. Applying $I=2000(0.06)(3)$ once would calculate simple interest on the original principal for all three years instead.

Keep full precision through the working, then round the final balance to \$2382.03. The third year's interest is $134.832$ before rounding, and the unrounded balance is $2382.032$.

Next reveal the right-hand column. Ask how each interest-and-addition calculation can be written as one multiplication. Increasing the current balance by 6% is the same as multiplying it by 1.06. Compare corresponding years side by side.

Before the final reveal, ask how to write the three multiplications more compactly. Three annual compounding periods give three factors of 1.06. Lead into the next slide: replace 2000 by $P$, the 6% rate by $r\%$, and three periods by $n$ periods. The exponent counts compounding periods.
:::
